docs.title: Home
docs.text: A lightweight CLI distributed version control system designed to help legal professionals easily view and understand different versions of .docx files.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
• While there are many different version control systems, many struggle to track diffs in .docx files because they are binary. SCCS solves this by converting .docx files to HTML using Mammoth, and keeping a HTML version of each commit.
  • SCCS is for professionals frequently working with Word Documents who are searching for a better way to track and view file changes of contracts.
  • Currently, most version control for contracts is just multiple versions of mostly identical files, emailed back and forth between people. Storing a folder of history metadata, hidden from the user simplifies this process. It also cleanly shows diff between version of a file, as opposed to between different files.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
CLI Commands:

sccs branch - Create a new branch, delete, or list branches.
sccs clone - Clone a hosted SCCS repository with a URL.
sccs commit - Commit changes to the repository.
sccs config - Configure a repository's data value (remote, name, email)
sccs diff - Show differences between the current document and a past commit.
sccs help - Print this help message.
sccs init - Initialize a new SCCS repository.
sccs log - Print a list of past commits for the current branch.
sccs open - Open a commit file and update the current document.
sccs publish - Publish a local repository to a hosting service.
sccs pull - Pull changes from a remote repository and merge them into the local repository.
sccs push - Push changes from the local repository to a remote repository.
sccs revert - Revert the current document to the specified commit.
sccs reset - Delete all uncommitted changes.
sccs switch - Switch between document branches.
sccs status - Check the status of the current document for uncommitted changes.
sccs merge - Merge the entered branch into the current branch.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Clone the Git Repository
git clone https://github.com/SCCS-HQ/legal-contract-version-control.git

# Install all required dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: MacOS / Linux
docs.text:
# Copy all repo CLI files to /usr/local/bin/
sudo cp commands/* /usr/local/bin/

# Make SCCS file executable
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/sccs

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text: By participating in this project, you agree to abide by our Code of Conduct. Please be respectful, welcoming, and constructive in all interactions.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or higher. Download here.
  • All dependencies defined in requirements.txt. Install with pip install -r requirements.txt.
  • Git — for version control and submitting changes.
  • A GitHub account — to open issues and submit pull requests.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Clone the Git Repository
git clone https://github.com/SCCS-HQ/legal-contract-version-control.git

# Move into the project directory
cd legal-contract-version-control

# Install all required dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Project Setup
docs.text: SCCS is a CLI tool. After cloning and installing dependencies, make the commands available on your system:

docs.title: macOS / Linux
docs.text:
# Copy all repo CLI files to /usr/local/bin/
sudo cp commands/* /usr/local/bin/

# Make the SCCS entrypoint executable
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/sccs

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Setup instructions for Windows are still TBA. If you get SCCS running on Windows, please consider opening a PR to document the steps!

Note: Repositories or clones created with older SCCS versions cannot currently be migrated to newer SCCS versions. Please re-clone the repository or re-initialize SCCS instead.

docs.title: Find Something to Do
docs.text:
The easiest way to get started is to browse the Issues tab:

  • Look for issues labeled good first issue if you're new to the project.
  • Check for issues labeled help wanted for tasks we'd love community help with.
  • If you have an idea that isn't already tracked, open a new issue to discuss it before starting work.

docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository on GitHub.
  2. Clone your fork locally: bash git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/legal-contract-version-control.git cd legal-contract-version-control
  3. Create a branch for your work (see Commit Guidelines for naming): bash git checkout -b feature/my-new-feature
  4. Make your changes, keeping them focused and well-tested.
  5. Commit your changes following the guidelines below.
  6. Push your branch to your fork: bash git push origin feature/my-new-feature
  7. Open a Pull Request against the main branch of the upstream repository.

docs.title: Commit Guidelines
docs.text:
• Write clear, descriptive commit messages in the imperative mood (e.g., Add diff command for tracked files, not Added diff command).
  • Keep commits focused — one logical change per commit is easier to review.
  • Reference the related issue where applicable (e.g., Fix #42: handle empty document on commit).

docs.title: Branch Naming
docs.text:
Use a short, descriptive prefix:

Prefix Purpose feature/ New features or enhancements fix/ Bug fixes docs/ Documentation changes test/ Adding or updating tests refactor/ Code changes that don't change behavior

docs.title: Pull Requests
docs.text:
• Target the main branch of the upstream repository.
  • Fill out the PR template and describe what changed and why.
  • Link any related issues (e.g., Closes #42).
  • Ensure your code follows the existing style and that the CLI commands still work as expected.
  • Be responsive to review feedback — reviews are how we keep the codebase healthy.

docs.title: Reporting Bugs & Suggesting Features
docs.text:
Before opening a new issue, please search existing issues to avoid duplicates.

  • Bugs: Include steps to reproduce, expected behavior, actual behavior, your OS, and Python version.
  • Features: Describe the problem you're trying to solve and propose a solution if you have one.

Use the appropriate issue label (bug or enhancement) when creating the issue.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text:
If you get stuck or have questions, feel free to open an issue or reach out. We're happy to help you get your contribution merged!

Thank you for helping make SCCS better!

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: This documentation covers all available commands in the SCCS (Specialized Contract Control System) — a version control and diffing tool designed specifically for .docx legal contracts and documents.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Branch — Create, delete, and manage branches
  2. Clone — Clone a hosted repository
  3. Commit — Commit changes to the repository
  4. Config — Configure repository settings
  5. Diff — Display differences between commits
  6. Help — Display help information
  7. Init — Initialize a new repository
  8. Log — View commit history
  9. Merge — Merge branches together
  10. Open — Open a historical commit
  11. Publish — Publish repository to a hosting service
  12. Pull — Pull changes from remote repository
  13. Push — Push changes to remote repository
  14. Reset — Discard uncommitted changes
  15. Revert — Revert to a previous commit
  16. Status — Check for uncommitted changes
  17. Switch — Switch between branches

docs.title: Branch
docs.text: Create, delete, and list branches within your repository.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs branch <subcommand> [branch-name]

docs.title: create
docs.text:
Creates a new branch based on the current branch.

Usage: sccs branch create <branch-name>

Arguments:

  • <branch-name> — The name of the new branch to create

Behavior:

  • The new branch inherits all commits and history from the current branch
  • The newly created branch becomes the current branch
  • Branch names are sanitized to be valid directory names
  • Fails if a branch with the same name already exists

Example:

sccs branch create feature-update

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
Deletes an existing branch.

Usage: sccs branch delete <branch-name>

Arguments:

  • <branch-name> — The name of the branch to delete

Behavior:

  • Cannot delete the current branch (switch branches first)
  • Removes the branch from all metadata files
  • Fails if the branch does not exist
  • Changes are rolled back if deletion fails partway through

Example:

sccs branch delete old-version

docs.title: list
docs.text:
Displays all branches in the repository, marking the current branch with an asterisk.

Usage: sccs branch list

Arguments: None

Behavior:

  • Lists all branches in alphabetical order
  • Marks the current branch with * (current)
  • Other branches are prefixed with spaces

Example Output:

Branches:

  backup-branch
  feature-update
* main (current)

docs.title: Clone
docs.text: Download a hosted SCCS repository to your local machine.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs clone <url>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • <url> — The hosted repository URL (must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL)

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Automatically appends /clone to the URL if not present
  • Downloads and extracts the repository as a zip file
  • Creates a folder named after the repository in the current directory
  • Requires internet connectivity

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs clone https://api.example.com/legal-contracts

docs.title: Commit
docs.text: Save the current document changes as a new commit in the repository.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs commit "<commit-message>"

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • <commit-message> — A descriptive message describing the changes (required, cannot be empty)

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Creates a snapshot of the current document state
  • Generates a unique SHA-256 commit hash
  • Stores both .docx and .html versions
  • Commits are immutable once created
  • Records the author name and email (from config) and timestamp

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs commit "Updated Section 3 terms and conditions"

docs.title: Config
docs.text: Configure repository-specific settings.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs config <key> <value>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• <key> — The configuration key to set (see valid keys below)
  • <value> — The value to assign to the key

docs.title: name
docs.text:
Your name, used to identify commits you make.

Example:

sccs config name "John Doe"

docs.title: email
docs.text:
Your email address, used alongside your name in commit metadata.

Example:

sccs config email "john.doe@example.com"

docs.title: remote
docs.text:
The URL of the remote hosting service for push/pull operations.

Example:

sccs config remote https://api.example.com/repos

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• The remote value is automatically formatted to end with /repos/<repository-name>
  • Remote URLs must start with http:// or https://
  • Configuration values are stored in .sccs/config/config.json

docs.title: Diff
docs.text: Generate an HTML redline document showing differences between two commits.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs diff <commit-hash>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • <commit-hash> — The commit SHA hash (or first 10 characters) to compare against the current document

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Compares the historical commit with the current document
  • Creates an HTML file named redline.html in the current directory
  • Color-codes changes:
  • Deleted content appears with a "deleted" class (typically red strikethrough)
  • Inserted content appears with an "inserted" class (typically green highlight)
  • Removes inline formatting tags to avoid duplication in the diff
  • Can be opened in any web browser

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs diff 5a3b2c1d9e

docs.title: Help
docs.text: Display a list of all available SCCS commands.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs help

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Prints a summary of all available commands with brief descriptions
  • Useful as a quick reference guide

docs.title: Init
docs.text: Initialize a new SCCS repository for a .docx document.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs init <file-path>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • <file-path> — The path to the .docx file to initialize

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Creates the .sccs directory structure
  • Prompts for your name and email (used for commits)
  • Moves the document into a repository directory
  • Creates an initial commit with the document's current state
  • Initializes the main branch
  • Fails if the file has already been initialized or is not a .docx file

docs.title: Prompted Inputs
docs.text:
• name — Your full name
  • email — Your email address

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs init contract.docx

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Enter your name: Jane Smith
Enter your email: jane.smith@example.com
SCCS initialization complete.

docs.title: Log
docs.text: Display the commit history for the current branch.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs log

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Shows all commits in the current branch in reverse chronological order
  • Displays for each commit:
  • First 10 characters of the SHA hash
  • Commit author
  • Timestamp (ISO 8601 format)
  • Commit message
  • Each commit entry is separated by a dashed line

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
------------------------------
Commit File: 5a3b2c1d9e
Author: John Doe <john.doe@example.com>
Date: 2025-01-15T14:30:45.123456
Message: Updated liability clause
------------------------------

docs.title: Merge
docs.text: Merge another branch into the current branch.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs merge <branch-name>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • <branch-name> — The name of the branch to merge into the current branch

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Copies all commit history from the source branch to the current branch
  • Overwrites the current document with the source branch's latest version
  • Creates an automatic commit with a merge message
  • Cannot merge a branch into itself
  • Fails if the target branch does not exist
  • Requires no uncommitted changes

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs merge feature-update

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Successfully merged branch 'feature-update' into branch 'main'.

docs.title: Open
docs.text: Open a historical commit and update the current document to that version.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs open <commit-hash>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • <commit-hash> — The SHA hash (or first 10 characters) of the commit to open

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Displays a confirmation prompt before overwriting the current document
  • Replaces the current document with the selected historical version
  • Does not create a new commit (use after this if you want to save changes)
  • Fails if the commit does not exist
  • Requires no uncommitted changes

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs open 5a3b2c1d9e

docs.title: Confirmation Prompt
docs.text:
Are you sure you want to overwrite './contract.docx' with the contents of 'commit_5a3b2c1d9e'?
This action will replace the current content of the .docx file. (Y/N):

docs.title: Publish
docs.text: Publish the repository to a remote hosting service.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs publish

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Requires a remote URL configured via sccs config remote
  • Compresses the entire repository into a zip file
  • Sends the zip to the remote server via HTTP POST
  • Resets the current branch to main before publishing
  • Provides status code and confirmation message

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs publish

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Publishing repository to https://api.example.com/repos/contract...

Status Code: 200

Repository published successfully to https://api.example.com/repos/contract

docs.title: Pull
docs.text: Fetch and merge changes from a remote repository.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs pull

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Requires a remote URL configured via sccs config remote
  • Compares local commits with remote commits
  • Downloads only the missing commit objects
  • Merges remote history into the local repository
  • Updates the current document to match the remote

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs pull

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Pulling repository from https://api.example.com/repos/contract...

Status Code: 200

Repository pulled successfully from https://api.example.com/repos/contract

docs.title: Push
docs.text: Send local changes to a remote repository.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs push

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Requires a remote URL configured via sccs config remote
  • Compares local and remote commit objects
  • Uploads only commits that the remote is missing
  • Fails if the local repository is missing commits from the remote
  • Clears the updated_branches list after successful push

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs push

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Pushing changes to remote repository at https://api.example.com/repos/contract...

Status code: 200

Changes pushed successfully to https://api.example.com/repos/contract/push

docs.title: Reset
docs.text: Discard all uncommitted changes and restore the document to the latest commit.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs reset

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Replaces the current document with the latest commit on the current branch
  • Fails if there are no uncommitted changes to reset
  • Irreversible operation (use with caution)

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs reset

docs.title: Output
docs.text: All uncommitted changes have been deleted. The document has been reset to the latest commit.

docs.title: Revert
docs.text: Create a new commit that reverts the document to a previous commit state.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs revert <commit-hash>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • <commit-hash> — The SHA hash (or first 10 characters) of the commit to revert to

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Reverts the document to the state of the specified commit
  • Automatically creates a new commit with message Revert to commit '<hash>'
  • The revert is saved as a new commit in the history
  • Different from reset because it preserves history (creates a new commit)
  • Fails if the specified commit does not exist
  • Requires no uncommitted changes

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs revert 5a3b2c1d9e

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Document successfully reverted to commit '5a3b2c1d' on commit '8f4e9d2c1b'.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Check for uncommitted changes in the current document.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs status

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Compares the current document with the latest commit
  • Uses binary hash comparison (detects any changes, no matter how small)
  • Prints one of two messages:
  • "Uncommitted changes detected." — if the document has been modified
  • "No uncommitted changes detected." — if the document matches the latest commit

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs status

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Uncommitted changes detected.

docs.title: Switch
docs.text: Switch between branches.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sccs switch <branch-name>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • <branch-name> — The name of the branch to switch to

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Updates metadata to mark the specified branch as current
  • Replaces the current document with the latest commit from the target branch
  • Fails if the target branch does not exist
  • Fails if there are uncommitted changes (commit or reset first)
  • The switched branch becomes the active branch for all future operations

docs.title: Example
docs.text: sccs switch feature-update

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Successfully switched to branch 'feature-update'.

docs.title: 1. Initialize a New Repository
docs.text: sccs init my_contract.docx

docs.title: 2. Configure Your Identity
docs.text:
sccs config name "Your Name"
sccs config email "your.email@example.com"

docs.title: 3. Create Your First Commit
docs.text: sccs commit "Initial version of contract"

docs.title: 4. Check Status
docs.text: sccs status

docs.title: 5. View Commit History
docs.text: sccs log

docs.title: 6. Create and Switch to a New Branch
docs.text:
sccs branch create revision-v2
sccs switch revision-v2

docs.title: 7. Make Changes and Commit
docs.text:
# (Edit your document)
sccs commit "Updated payment terms"

docs.title: 8. View Differences
docs.text: sccs diff <previous-commit-hash>

docs.title: 9. Merge Back to Main
docs.text:
sccs switch main
sccs merge revision-v2

docs.title: 10. Configure Remote and Push
docs.text:
sccs config remote https://api.example.com
sccs push

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• All commit hashes are SHA-256 hexadecimal strings; only the first 10 characters are typically needed
  • Document .docx files are automatically converted to .html for diffing purposes
  • All timestamps are stored in ISO 8601 format
  • Branch names and document names are sanitized to be valid directory names
  • The .sccs folder contains all version control metadata and should not be manually edited
